title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 140 (Removal, resignation of auditor and giving of special notice)

content.overview: The auditor appointed under section 139 may be removed from his office before the expiry of his term only by a special resolution of the company, after obtaining the previous approval of the Central Government in that behalf in the prescribed manner. The auditor who has resigned from the company shall file within a period of thirty days from the date of resignation, a statement in the prescribed form with the company and the Registrar.
content.glance: Removal before term needs special resolution and previous Central Government approval; resignation requires the prescribed statement within thirty days.
content.study:
## Section 140 — Removal, resignation of auditor

**Removal before term.** Only by special resolution of the company after previous approval of the Central Government in the prescribed manner.

**Resignation.** Auditor who resigns files a statement in the prescribed form with the company and the Registrar within thirty days of resignation. For a Government company or a company owned or controlled by the Government, the statement also goes to the Comptroller and Auditor-General.

**Special notice.** Section 140(4) deals with a resolution at an AGM appointing a person other than the retiring auditor, or providing that the retiring auditor shall not be re-appointed; special notice is required.

**Tribunal.** The Tribunal may also order a change of auditor on application in the circumstances in the section, including fraud.

Appointment for the term is section 139.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.
